nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Sun drives growth in the gorge forests, where steep rock slopes create warm and cool pockets side by side.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Rain feeds the forests and the karst springs and streams that run down into the gorge.

nodes.name: Danube river
nodes.desc: The Danube cuts the long Iron Gates gorge here. Dams raised the river and formed a large reservoir with new wetlands along its edge.

nodes.name: Soil & leaf litter
nodes.desc: Forest litter and thin karst soils hold the nutrients the trees draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Downy oak & other oaks
nodes.desc: Wikipedia lists downy oak among the relict tree species of the park. Acorns feed many forest animals.

nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: A common broadleaf forest tree of the Balkan hills, producing beechnuts that forest animals eat.

nodes.name: Turkish hazel
nodes.desc: A Tertiary relict tree named by Wikipedia among the park's notable plants. Its nuts are food for small forest animals.

nodes.name: False acacia
nodes.desc: An introduced tree that is the most recorded plant near the park in GBIF. It grows thickly on disturbed ground.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: Feeds on grass, leaves, berries and young shoots. Where it is common it is the preferred prey of the Eurasian lynx.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots through forest floors for nuts, plants and small animals. Wikipedia says deer and boar are common around the park.

nodes.name: Yellow-necked mouse
nodes.desc: A seed-eating forest rodent and a staple prey of martens, hedgehogs and birds of prey.

nodes.name: Edible dormouse
nodes.desc: A tree-living rodent that eats nuts, seeds and fruit in broadleaf forest.

nodes.name: Eurasian jay
nodes.desc: A woodland crow that eats acorns and other seeds along with insects, and is among the most recorded forest birds nearby.

nodes.name: Common wood pigeon
nodes.desc: Eats seeds, buds, leaves and acorns in woodland and fields.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A bird of prey that hunts small mammals and birds from perches over forest edges and clearings.

nodes.name: Beech marten
nodes.desc: An omnivorous mustelid that hunts rodents and birds and also eats fruit.

nodes.name: Southern white-breasted hedgehog
nodes.desc: A ground-foraging insect and small-animal eater of woodland edges and scrub.

nodes.name: Griffon vulture
nodes.desc: A large scavenger that feeds on carrion and nests on cliffs. It is the most recorded bird near the park in GBIF.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever omnivore that scavenges carcasses and also takes small animals.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: The park's top predator, with a small population reported in the 2020s. It prefers roe deer where they are common.
